No purchases dated after Aug 21 have surfaced yet in the most recent filings reviewed, so the buying streak is confirmed through late August but not yet re-verified for the first days of September.
signals.institutional_buying: New institutional activity has emerged following the Aug 12 data: MarketBeat's institutional-ownership tracker shows fresh 13F-linked positions from Bank of America Corp DE (224,412 shares, ~$1.02M, reported 8/17/2026), BlackRock Inc. (179,850 shares, ~$815K, reported 8/7/2026), and smaller stakes from Global Retirement Partners and Westmount Partners -- institutional buyers have outnumbered sellers 13-to-2 over the trailing year with roughly $14.08M in institutional inflows versus $465.73K in outflows, though absolute institutional ownership remains low given the stock's small float.
catalysts: NEO100 Phase 2a hit its primary PFS-6 endpoint (48.9% vs a 20% historical benchmark, p=0.0047) in recurrent IDH1-mutant high-grade glioma, announced Aug 12, 2026, and management separately disclosed a 26.09-month median overall survival figure for the program, both reinforcing the strength of the data set (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/12/3343608/0/en/neonc-technologies-reports-positive-topline-phase-2a-results-for-intranasal-neo100-in-recurrent-idh1-mutant-high-grade-glioma.html)

NeOnc has stated it plans to request a Type B FDA meeting to discuss a potential registrational trial design and approval pathway for NEO100; as of the most recent reporting the meeting request has not yet been confirmed as submitted and no meeting date has been disclosed, so this remains a pending near-term catalyst rather than a completed one (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/NeOnc+Technologies+Holdings+Reports+Positive+Phase+2a+NEO100+Results+and+Plans+FDA+Meeting+on+Potential+Registrational+Path+for+Brain+Cancer+Treatment)

NEO212 separately received FDA feedback indicating a potential accelerated-approval pathway alongside Phase 2 CMC clearance, and the company holds UAE IND approvals spanning NEO100 and NEO212 across adult and pediatric programs
The company raised approximately $20 million in capital in August 2026 but continues to disclose a 'going concern' warning in its 10-Q, a financing-risk factor to weigh against the clinical progress
analyst_moves: Stonegate Capital Partners updated coverage following the Phase 2a data and highlighted the 26.09-month median overall survival figure (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/NTHI/stonegate-capital-partners-updates-coverage-on-ne-onc-technologies-kuhjbbednz3a.html)

Existing Street coverage remains constructive with Buy ratings from BTIG ($15 target, reiterated May 26), Alliance Global Partners ($13 target, initiated May 19) and Maxim Group ($20 target, initiated May 18), against consensus price targets implying substantial upside from the current ~$4.70-4.80 share price; Weiss Ratings maintains a contrarian Sell view (downgraded June 24)

watchlist.thesis: NTHI remains the standout name on the board. The Aug 12 Phase 2a hit for NEO100 was a genuine, statistically robust catalyst, and unlike a typical spike-and-fade biotech pop, both co-CEOs kept adding shares in the open market with their own cash through at least Aug 21 -- Heshmatpour and Chen have now strung together six straight months without a single sale, spanning well before and continuing after the data readout, which is the exact quiet-accumulation signature this screen is built to find. Fresh institutional interest from BlackRock and Bank of America filed in the days after the catalyst adds a second confirming pillar, and the planned FDA Type B meeting on a registrational pathway is a credible, well-defined next catalyst. The stock's retracement from its post-data spike into a $4.60-5.10-ish consolidation range, on volume still well above its pre-catalyst base, looks like healthy digestion rather than a failed breakout.
watchlist.risks: The FDA Type B meeting has only been described as planned, not yet confirmed as scheduled or held, so the next major regulatory catalyst still carries timing uncertainty. The company's 10-Q continues to flag going-concern risk despite the recent $20 million raise, and further dilutive financing is a realistic possibility for a company at this stage. No insider purchases have been confirmed in filings reviewed after Aug 21, so continued buying into September should be reconfirmed in the next screening pass. As a sub-$150M market-cap name with thin average daily volume (under 100,000 shares), the stock remains highly volatile and could gap sharply on any incremental FDA or trial news.

watchlist.name: Capricor Therapeutics, Inc.
watchlist.volume_trend: Volume running well above average (6.27M vs 3.07M shares) driven by the FDA review-extension news and subsequent dual analyst upgrades, indicating active repositioning rather than quiet accumulation.

catalysts: FDA extended the PDUFA target action date for deramiocel's BLA in Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months, from Aug 22 to Nov 22, 2026, after accepting a major amendment that includes 24-month HOPE-3 open-label extension data and a refined proposed indication focused on upper-limb function (https://www.capricor.com/investors/news-events/press-releases/detail/354/capricor-therapeutics-announces-extension-of-pdufa-target)

CBER's acceptance of the amendment, rather than a rejection or additional Advisory Committee meeting, was read by the market as a sign the review is still progressing constructively following the negative July 2026 Advisory Committee vote

Litigation overhang persists: securities-law investigations (e.g., Lowey Dannenberg) tied to Capricor's disclosures around the FDA panel vote remain unresolved, alongside the earlier-filed lawsuit against Nippon Shinyaku
analyst_moves: Oppenheimer upgraded Capricor on Aug 25, 2026 citing the regulatory update (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/oppenheimer-upgrades-capricor-stock-rating-on-regulatory-update-93CH-4875167)

Piper Sandler upgraded Capricor on Sept 1, 2026 citing FDA review progress, a fresh positive signal since the prior evening's screen (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/piper-sandler-upgrades-capricor-stock-rating-on-fda-review-progress-93CH-4883850)

watchlist.thesis: Capricor's PDUFA extension to Nov 22, 2026 -- rather than an outright rejection following July's negative Advisory Committee vote -- has been read constructively by the Street, evidenced by back-to-back analyst upgrades from Oppenheimer and Piper Sandler (the latter as recent as Sept 1). This is a real regulatory catalyst that has stabilized sentiment after a brutal year-to-date decline, and the stock is consolidating well above its August lows. The screen's insider-buying pillar remains empty and litigation risk from the securities-law investigations is unresolved, keeping this a core watch rather than a high-conviction name until deramiocel's regulatory picture clears further or insiders start buying.
watchlist.risks: Deramiocel's BLA still requires FDA to weigh new HOPE-3 open-label extension data and a narrowed indication after an adverse Advisory Committee vote, so approval is far from assured by the new Nov 22 date. Ongoing securities-litigation investigations tied to disclosures around the panel vote add legal overhang. No insider has bought shares despite the recent positive catalysts, and the stock remains down sharply from its 52-week high, reflecting a still-fragile risk/reward.
